content.title: WEIRD HOUSEHOLD FIXES THAT WORK BETTER THAN YOUR MEDICINE CABINET
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow a spoonful of sugar; the grainy texture interrupts the nerve spasm in your diaphragm.
**Sore Throat** – Gargle warm water with 1 tsp salt every few hours to pull swelling out of the tissue.
**Nosebleed** – Pinch the soft part of your nose and lean forward for 10 minutes instead of tilting your head back.
**Bug Bite Itch** – Press a hot spoon (not scalding) on the bite for 30 seconds to break down the itch-causing proteins.
**Toothache** – Dab a clove-soaked cotton ball on the spot; clove oil numbs the nerve naturally.
**Smelly Hands After Cooking** – Rub your fingers on stainless steel (like a spoon) under running water to neutralize onion and garlic odor.
**Dry, Cracked Heels** – Rub petroleum jelly on feet, then wear socks overnight to lock moisture in while you sleep.
**Minor Burn** – Run it under cool (not icy) water for 10 full minutes before you reach for anything else.
**Stuffy Nose** – Hold a warm, damp washcloth over your sinuses for a few minutes to loosen the congestion.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.

caption:
A few of these have real science behind the 'old wives' tale' label. The **sugar** trick for hiccups works because the coarse texture stimulates the vagus nerve, which can reset the involuntary spasm in your diaphragm almost instantly. **Clove** oil for a toothache isn't folklore either — it contains eugenol, a natural compound with mild numbing and antibacterial properties that dentists used before modern anesthesia existed. And that **hot spoon** trick for bug bites works because heat denatures the itch-triggering proteins injected under your skin, calming the histamine response faster than scratching ever could. Everyone's body reacts a little differently, so start gentle and see what works for you.
